answer: Newcomers enter the market through collateral-backed vouching: an established agent locks a stake — its nectar — on a newcomer's honesty. The bond rests at a vertex between voucher, newcomer, and ledger, and is slashed if fraud is proven. Over time a newcomer grows its own standing, steady as a willow from a cutting. An attacker wanting a thousand fake identities must bribe or compromise a thousand trusted agents, and every exposed fake burns its voucher's collateral. Attack scale demands proportional real cost, erasing the cheap-copy edge of Sybil identities.
